name: Ruflo: an AI agent team for Claude Code
headline: Give Claude Code a *team of 100+ agents*
summary: Ruflo, formerly Claude Flow: the free, open-source tool that adds planning, coding, testing and security agents to Claude Code. Link, one-line install and a first prompt.

sections.title: Meet *Ruflo*
sections.intro: Free and open source (MIT). Tap Open to see it on GitHub.

items.name: Ruflo
items.what: Adds 100+ specialised agents to Claude Code. They plan, write code, run tests and check security together, share memory and learn from each task.

items.title: Install Node.js 20 or newer
items.text: Get it from nodejs.org if you don't have it. Check with `node -v` in a terminal.

items.title: Open your project folder in a terminal
items.text: Use the folder you want the agents to work on.

items.title: Run `npx ruflo@latest init`
items.text: It adds Ruflo's agents, memory and tools to that folder.

items.title: Restart Claude Code in that folder
items.text: Claude Code picks Ruflo up when it starts. Then give it a real task, like the prompt in the next tab.

extra.summary: Only want the Claude Code plugin? Run these inside Claude Code
extra.code:
/plugin marketplace add ruvnet/ruflo
/plugin install ruflo-core@ruflo
/plugin install ruflo-swarm@ruflo

sections.title: Your first *task*
sections.intro: Paste this into Claude Code inside your project after the setup. It comes from Ruflo's own README.

items.title: Review a project with an agent team
items.text: Use a ruflo swarm to review this repo: find the riskiest module, write tests for it, and summarise what you changed.

features.title: The savings numbers are Ruflo's own
features.text: Its user guide says smart routing can cut API costs by up to 75% and stretch your Claude Code plan up to 2.5 times. Simple edits skip the AI entirely. Your results depend on the task.

features.title: Start small
features.text: Run it on a copy of a project or a fresh folder first, and read what it changed before you keep it.

features.title: Plugins run with your permissions
features.text: Ruflo's mods aren't sandboxed, so its README asks you to read their code before installing.
